stem: A nurse is teaching an adult strategies to prevent constipation. Which recommendation is most appropriate?

options.A: Increase fiber gradually, drink adequate fluids as appropriate, stay active, and respond to the urge to have a bowel movement during the day.
options.B: Restrict fluid intake, decrease dietary fiber, and delay bowel movements when inconvenient so the colon can adapt to less frequent elimination.
options.C: Use a stimulant laxative every day as the first prevention strategy, even when diet, fluids, activity, and bowel habits have not been addressed.
options.D: Avoid regular physical activity and reduce fruit and vegetable intake because both can increase intestinal motility and worsen constipation.

rationale: NIDDK recommends adequate dietary fiber, sufficient liquids, regular physical activity, and regular bowel habits to help prevent and manage constipation. Ignoring the urge to defecate can contribute to constipation. Option A best reflects these measures. The other choices reduce fiber or fluids, reduce activity, delay bowel movements, or make daily stimulant-laxative use the default first strategy without first addressing basic measures.
educational_objective: Teach first-line lifestyle and bowel-habit measures that help prevent constipation.
source_organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)
source_version_date: Current NIDDK web guidance; page last reviewed May 2018
source_locator: Sections 'How can I prevent constipation?' and home treatment: adequate fiber, fluids, regular physical activity, and regular bowel habits; related Symptoms & Causes page notes ignoring the urge to have a bowel movement as a contributor.
source_claim_supported: NIDDK supports fiber, fluids, physical activity, and regular bowel habits for constipation prevention; delaying defecation can contribute to constipation.

source_original.stem: A nurse is teaching an adult strategies to prevent constipation. Which recommendation is most appropriate?

options.A: Increase fiber gradually, drink adequate fluids as appropriate, stay active, and respond to the urge to have a bowel movement during the day.
options.B: Restrict fluid intake, decrease dietary fiber, and delay bowel movements when inconvenient so the colon can adapt to less frequent elimination.
options.C: Use a stimulant laxative every day as the first prevention strategy, even when diet, fluids, activity, and bowel habits have not been addressed.
options.D: Avoid regular physical activity and reduce fruit and vegetable intake because both can increase intestinal motility and worsen constipation.

source_original.rationale: NIDDK recommends adequate fiber, sufficient fluids, regular physical activity, and healthy bowel habits for constipation prevention and management. Option A is correct. Option B reduces both fluid and fiber intake and encourages delaying defecation, all of which work against prevention. Option C makes a daily stimulant laxative the first strategy before basic measures have been addressed. Option D removes physical activity and reduces fiber-rich produce even though those measures can support bowel function.
source_original.source_detail: NIDDK — Treatment for Constipation: increase fiber, drink adequate liquids when appropriate, engage in regular physical activity, and establish healthy bowel habits/respond to the urge to defecate; stimulant laxatives are not the default first prevention measure. Current NIDDK constipation guidance at cited federal URL; live content rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort: mobility, positioning, skin integrity, elimination and nonpharmacologic comfort activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the construct and answer key. Tightened the rationale to the directly supported NIDDK prevention measures and separated the 'respond to urge' claim to NIDDK's causes guidance rather than implying it appears verbatim on the treatment page.

audit_findings.currentness: Live NIDDK content rechecked 2026-08-16; page review date is older but no superseding NIDDK guidance was found.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Prevention/home-treatment sections support fiber, fluids, activity and bowel habits; NIDDK causes page supports avoiding delayed defecation.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No universal fluid quantity, fiber gram target, or laxative regimen was added.

distractor_audit.C: Inappropriately makes stimulant laxative use the default first strategy.
distractor_audit.D: Opposes recommended activity and fiber intake.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A is compatible with the full prevention framework.
audit_findings.blueprint: Fits elimination and nonpharmacologic care in Basic Care and Comfort.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Second pass confirmed no unsupported daily timing or numerical intake targets remain.
